# Opus 5 — ultracode

> An exceptionally well-engineered static Pokédex: 32,737 lines across 146 files with zero `any`, zero suppression comments and zero TODO markers, strict TS gating the build, a pure-function domain layer (types, damage, stats, evolution, coverage, filtering) that never imports React, and a dependency-free build pipeline that resolves 638k learnset rows and 117k encounter rows into 6,032 static shards in 2 seconds. The core logic is not decorative — the type chart is the real veekun efficacy table with era-aware past overrides, the damage engine reproduces the cartridge's exact floor/pokeRound nesting and convolves full roll distributions for nHKO odds, the stat formulas handle both classic traps (Shedinja base-1 HP, nature applied after the floor), and evolution is a genuine recursive branching tree with cross-chain root resolution. Coverage is complete: 1025/1025 species reachable at runtime with no console errors. The adjudication pass sustained most of the auditor's downgrades because the *feature* tier has a consistent pattern the axis scores hide — a large number of surfaces are correct, complete and one step short of the depth the top anchor demands (filters that filter but never count or negate, sorts whose metric is never displayed, breeding and dex text that stop at the raw CSV columns, a team builder missing named teams, Showdown interop and damage preview). Three defects are outright bugs rather than shallowness: alternate-form sprites are keyed off the wrong id space so every one of 235 non-default form rows silently renders a different Pokémon; index-entry generation comes from the species row so generation filtering is wrong for all regional and Mega forms even though the builder already reads the correct column for the detail page; and the command palette's landing-page entry point throws an uncaught TypeError while 5 of its 18 page results 404 against a stale hardcoded route table. Still the strongest submission in the field on engineering substance — the deductions are about the last mile, not the foundation.

## Strengths

- Domain logic is reference-grade: exact cartridge damage nesting with pokeRound and full 16-roll KO-chance convolution, correct HP/stat formulas with the Shedinja and nature-order traps handled, and a defensive profile that re-types through the selected ability.
- Data pipeline is dependency-free and fast — `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/build-data.ts` runs with no node_modules at all, emitting 6,032 files / 41.3 MB in 2.0s from a shared quoted-CSV parser that handles embedded newlines and escapes.
- Zero runtime data API: the only fetch() in the client is /data/*, backed by a documented positional-tuple wire contract, an in-flight-deduping memory cache, adjacent-neighbour prefetch, and verified production cache headers (7d + 30d SWR on data, immutable 1y on media, HTMLRewriter OG injection on the shell, 33ms TTFB).
- Typing and layering discipline: zero `any`, zero ts-ignore/eslint-disable across 146 files, src/lib never imports src/components, all 812 imports resolve, and lazyWithRetry handles the stale-shell chunk-404 white screen almost nobody anticipates.
- Genuine feature breadth with real depth in the advanced dex filter (13 dimensions plus a trait list, all URL-allow-listed), the era-aware type chart, evolution branching, and the damage calculator.

## Weaknesses

- Alternate-form sprites use pokemon_forms.id in a path keyed by pokemon.id (builders/pokemon.ts:397) — Unown B renders Deoxys-Attack, and because the image exists no fallback fires; affects all 235 non-default form rows across 35 species.
- Index-entry generation is taken from the species row (builders/pokemon.ts:296) while the correct pokemon_forms version group is read for the detail page, so generation filtering misplaces every regional variant and Mega.
- The home hero CTA and 404 search button open the palette by dispatching a synthetic ⌘K on window, which throws in AppShell's keydown handler before reaching the ⌘K branch; the palette's page corpus is a stale hardcoded duplicate of the router with 5 dead routes.
- Worker API/OG layer has a live, publicly reachable 500: COLLECTIONS[segments[0]] is an unguarded prototype-chain lookup and decodeURIComponent is called raw despite a safeDecode helper existing, so /api/constructor and /pokemon/% return uncaught exceptions.
- public/sw.js hardcodes VERSION='pokedex-v1' with no build stamping while caching /data/* cacheFirst without revalidation, so the activate-purge can never fire and an installed client can serve last-deploy JSON indefinitely; package.json `build` also omits the data step while public/data is gitignored, and no builder asserts a species floor.
- The render layer is not decomposed to the standard of the logic layer — 14 top-level functions exceed 300 lines (DamageCalculator ~687 with a ~455-line JSX return) — and small contract drift has already started: PokedexFile declared twice, DatasetStats three times, three parallel URL-state codecs, a bypassed focus-trap hook, 9 dead exports.
- A broad band of features stop exactly at 'correct and complete': no per-type counts or negation in the type filter, sorted metrics never displayed on cards, breeding as a static CSV readout with non-clickable egg groups, English-only dex text with a non-deduped header count, no move search inside 909-row learnsets, favourites unstarrable from the browse grid, and a single unnamed team with no Showdown interop or damage preview.

## Standout

The build pipeline: `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/build-data.ts` resolves 638,321 learnset rows and 117,113 encounter rows into 6,032 static shards in 2.0 seconds with no node_modules installed at all — the builders import only node:fs and node:path — and the resulting positional-tuple wire format is declared once in src/types/data.ts and shared by both the generator and the app, so the entire 1,351-Pokémon dex ships as immutable CDN JSON with zero runtime API.

## Vendored source

The source in this directory is the code the model wrote, copied verbatim from [its repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-opus-5-ultracode) minus `node_modules`, build output, and generated data.

> 55 MB of PokéAPI data (public/data, 6032 files) and 41 MB of the upstream PokéAPI CSV dump (data-src, 180 files) stripped from the vendored source — it is data, not model-written code; regenerate with `npm run data` (the original repo keeps the CSV dump).

Canonical history and issues live in the [original repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-opus-5-ultracode). This is a scored snapshot for the benchmark.
